gaps.explanation: Statement lines come from the accrual Statement of Revenues, Expenses, and Changes in Net Position - Proprietary Funds p6 (printed p8): total operating revenues 549,781 + interest and investment revenue 147 = 549,928 (Water 374,813 + 114 = 374,927; Sewer 174,968 + 33 = 175,001; Other Proprietary Fund 0). Detail comes from the budgetary-basis (cash) Budgetary Comparison Schedules: Water p17 (printed p29) total revenues 398,146, Sewer p18 (p30) 189,163, Meter Deposit Fund p19 (p31) 2,550 = 589,859. Per fund: Water 398,146 - 374,927 = 23,219; Sewer 189,163 - 175,001 = 14,162; Meter Deposit 2,550 (customer deposits, cash only; the accrual statement prints 0 for the Other Proprietary Fund, cash flow p7 shows 2,550 cash received) = 39,931 = schedule excess. Both printed totals are correct on their own basis; no detail line is missing or duplicated.

Accrual statement p6: total operating expenses 488,506 (incl. depreciation 111,942) + interest expense 796 = 489,302 (Water 292,900; Sewer 195,606 + 796 = 196,402; Other 0). Budgetary-basis schedules: Water p17 total expenditures 289,002 (incl. capital outlay 74,289, no depreciation), Sewer p18 240,952 (incl. debt service 20,026 and capital outlay 64,203), Meter Deposit p19 2,150 = 532,104. Per fund: Water 289,002 - 292,900 = -3,898; Sewer 240,952 - 196,402 = 44,550; Meter Deposit 2,150 => 42,802 = schedule excess. Capital outlay and debt principal (budgetary) vs depreciation (accrual) explain the difference; no fix.
